draft.title: Local, national and global businesses
card: Businesses can be grouped by their geographic reach: the area where they sell and operate. Where their customers happen to come from does not decide it.
serves customers in one town, suburb or region, such as a bakery in Orange or a plumber who works around Hobart.
sells and operates across the whole country, often with outlets in every state, such as an Australian chain of hardware stores.
sells and operates in many countries, such as a car maker with factories and showrooms in Asia, Europe and the Americas.
draft.remember: Ask where the business sells and operates: one area, the whole country, or many countries.

a.q: Kai runs a dog-washing van that visits homes across Newcastle. Customers book online. How is his business classified by reach?
opts: Local, because it serves one city
National, because it travels between suburbs
Global, because it takes bookings online
National, because it is registered in Australia
a.why: Kai only sells and operates in Newcastle, so his business is local. Taking bookings online does not make it global, because he still only serves one area.
a.clue: Where does the van actually go?

b.q: Ruby runs a winery in the Barossa Valley. She sells wine only at her cellar door, and tourists from many countries visit. How is her business classified by reach?
opts: Local, because it sells only in its own area
Global, because its customers come from many countries
National, because tourists travel across Australia
Global, because wine is traded around the world
b.why: Ruby sells and operates only in the Barossa Valley, so the business is local. Her visitors come from overseas, but reach depends on where the business sells and operates, not where customers come from.
b.clue: Look at where Ruby sells, not who buys.

a.best: Local, because it serves one city

b.best: Local, because it sells only in its own area
